notes: Sourced from vivo's global English site (vivo.com/en). TRAP (c) per-colour dimensions AND mass: vivo publishes two full sets — Gray at 159.68 × 72.60 × 9.20 mm folded / 159.68 × 142.29 × 4.30 mm unfolded and 217 g, and White at 159.68 × 72.60 × 9.70 mm folded / 159.68 × 142.29 × 4.55 mm unfolded and 226 g. The recorded values are the GRAY (Titanium Gray) variant, which vivo lists first and which is the thinner/lighter of the two; the White variant is 0.50 mm thicker folded, 0.25 mm thicker unfolded and 9 g heavier, which matters for a CAD shell. The difference tracks the back material (glass fibre on Gray, glass on White). No hinge-side vs non-hinge-side split is published, so depth_at_hinge is null; height is identical in both states. DISPLAYS: vivo gives one Refresh Rate row, 'LTPO Adaptive Refresh Rate (1-120Hz)', and one Type row, 'AMOLED', both covering the two screens; refresh_hz is recorded as the 120 Hz maximum of that 1-120 Hz range for both. CREASE: vivo describes 'a rotating-sliding hinge' whose 'kinematic design reduces visible creases' but never names a crease profile (no teardrop/water-drop or U), so hinge.crease is null. FREE_STOP: unlike the X Fold3 Pro, the X Fold5 global pages contain no hover / free-angle / multi-angle claim at all, so hinge.free_stop is left null rather than carried over from the sibling model. No frame/mid-frame material is published, so materials.frame is null. Announce/release dates are not stated on either vivo global page, so both are null. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: displays[1].panel = 'OLED'; displays[1].refresh_hz = 120; hinge.type = 'book'; hinge.axis = 'long'.
